background: <background>MapTask dialogues involve a route giver guiding a follower using two similar but non-identical maps, and they cannot see each other's map. The giver has the route; some landmarks differ by name (lexical), existence (present on only one map), or multiplicity (appearing twice on one map). You are an expert annotator for reference expressions (REs). Now for each RE, you should annotate the speaker's intended and the addressee's interpreted landmarks using provided landmark IDs. Note that the speaker and addressee are determined by who produces and who receives the RE, not by the fixed giver/follower roles.</background>
task_description: <task_description>Annotate every RE listed in the target_ref_ids section using landmark IDs from the candidate inventory. Also fill in the boolean attributes: is_quantificational (from the speaker's perspective, whether the expression is used to check or deny the existence of a landmark rather than to refer to a specific one; the following four other attributes are from the addressee's perspective), is_specified (whether the addressee provides any response that shows they have noticed the RE rather than skipping or ignoring it), is_accommodated (whether the RE is successfully received and understood by the addressee, false if the addressee mishears, misunderstands, or ask for repetition), is_grounded (whether the RE is linked to any concrete landmark on the maps by the addressee), and is_imagined (optional, whether the grounded landmark exists only on the speaker's map). Base every decision strictly on the provided dialogue context and dialogue-act tags. Provided information includes: (1) dialogue context: dialogue transcript from the beginning of the dialogue until the end of the current transaction (a transaction is a series of moves from one point to another on the maps); (2) maps: both the giver's and follower's maps with map names at the bottom; (3) dialogue act tags: dialogue context annotated with dialogue acts; (4) landmark candidates: a list of all landmarks on both maps. Pick up IDs from the landmark_candidates section, and do not invent new IDs</task_description>
landmark_id_explanation: <landmark_id_explanation>Landmark ID syntax: <map-id>_<concept>#<ordinal>@<side>. <concept> is the landmark name from the original dataset; side ∈ {g,f} indicates which map the landmark is located on; ordinal (0 or 1) is used only when a concept appears twice on the same map; ordinal numbers are ordered from 0 to 1 by their occurrences from bottom to top on the same map, and the number is the same across maps at matching locations. For simultaneous multi-target references, join their IDs with '+'.</landmark_id_explanation>
annotation_rule: <annotation_rule>Follow the annotation workflow for each RE step by step: (0) Identify the speaker and the addressee from the sentence header; fill in the speaker's interpretation (intended landmark ID) first. Exception: if the speaker is querying or denying a landmark previously introduced by the addressee (e.g., "where is the running river?" / "I don't have the running river"), set the speaker's interpretation to empty (""). (1) Check is_quantificational: set it to true when the RE is used only to check or deny existence (e.g., "Do you have a parked van?" / "I don't have any roman baths" ); otherwise false. (2) Check is_specified: when not quantificational, determine if the addressee shows any uptake of the RE in the context, rather than ignoring or skipping it without reaction; if so, set is_specified=true, otherwise false. Exception——implicit reuse: if this expression was previously grounded between the interlocutors with no subsequent repair/denial, the current RE may be treated tacitly grounded; set is_specified=true, and at step (4) mark it as grounded. (3) Check is_accommodated: if specified, set is_accommodated=false when the addressee fails to process the RE, e.g., mishearing, confusion or requesting repetition; otherwise true. (4) Check is_grounded: when accommodated, set is_grounded=true only if the addressee links the RE to a specific landmark on the maps; otherwise false. (5) Check is_imagined: when grounded, set is_imagined=true if the addressee's interpretation is only on the speaker's map; otherwise false. (6) If grounded, fill in the landmark ID for the addressee's interpretation. (7) Provide a concise (<50 words) evidence-based reason summarizing the judgement in the reason field for each RE.</annotation_rule>
output_format:
<output_format>Return strict JSON only: {
  "dialogue_id": str,
 "landmark_reference_expressions": [
    {
      "ref_id_unif": str,
      "is_quantificational": bool,
      "is_specified": bool,
      "interpretations": {
        "is_accommodated": bool,
        "is_grounded": bool,
        "is_imagined": (optional) bool,
        "giver": str,
        "follower": str
      },
      "reason": str
    }
, ... ]
}</output_format>
